timestamp_conversion.signed_arithmetic: Compute signed i128 nanoseconds before magnitude/sign separation, so -2s+750ms is -1.25s and -1s+999999900ns is -100ns. i64 seconds times1e9 cannot overflow i128; Duration receives a <1e9 ns remainder.
timestamp_conversion.leap_seconds: The existing preceding-second plus >=1e9 ns representation becomes the following ordinary second, including crossing the Unix epoch. This is documented normalization; persisted Timestamp formatting and ordering are unchanged.
timestamp_conversion.range: SystemTime checked_add/checked_sub determine platform limits. u64/u32 conversions are fallible and no unchecked platform clock addition is introduced in the API.
timestamp_conversion.precision: SystemTime retains its platform-defined precision. New roundtrip vectors are100ns-aligned and do not claim arbitrary-nanosecond roundtrip fidelity on every OS.
timestamp_conversion.regression_coverage: Three new real Rust tests cover negative/positive fractional instants, explicit leap seconds, and both Timestamp calendar bounds using each platform's checked clock result; all prior Timestamp tests are byte-preserved.
timestamp_conversion.deduplication: The previously reviewed signed-nanosecond algorithm in common/rollout.rs is moved into the shared conversion API; the common fixture and six other call sites report an explicit conversion error instead of relying on a nonexistent From implementation.

fixture_errors.color_eyre_sites: Exactly three new conversion failure sites use std::io::Error::other: tui/lib.rs and the two named-session tests. These are compatible with their existing color_eyre::Result return types.
fixture_errors.anyhow_sites: App-server helpers/tests retain anyhow::Result and use anyhow errors. Parsing and file mutation errors still propagate.
fixture_errors.duration_fixture: Two one-hour Timestamp fixture increments use the existing checked_add API and descriptive expect assertions; fixture values and all lookup/archive assertions are retained.

box_and_import_repairs.owned_values: Both boxed ledger records and the boxed bootstrap custody are moved out once to existing owned-value APIs. Recovered optional receipt/evidence uses Option.map(Box::new), preserving None/Some and value identity.
box_and_import_repairs.imports: UnixStream and Duration imports resolve the actual reported names in the existing platform-specific test support. No production owner, custody guard, deadline or channel policy changes.

tui_shift.semantics: checked_add_signed applies the isize offset to both usize range bounds without truncating or reinterpreting negative values. Underflow/overflow returns None; the existing start>=end rejection remains. TextElement.map_range preserves the placeholder.
tui_shift.tests: Two real sibling-module tests compare complete TextElement values for positive/zero/negative shifts and check negative underflow, isize::MIN, usize overflow, isize::MAX and an empty range.
tui_shift.documentation: The bottom-pane AGENTS instruction is satisfied by the matching two-line module-doc description. The new test file is wired by cfg(test), an explicit path module and the existing recursive Rust source glob.

verification_scope: Independent frozen-byte binding, actual CI error review, production/API semantics and exact assertion preservation. No substitute model tests and no native execution.
remaining_gate: Actual project tests, formatting and required CI compilation must still run on the exact composed source; static review is not a native PASS.

known_followup_stage02.finding: Root reports the original unchanged epoch-minus1ns SystemTime test quantizes to epoch on Windows, producing seconds0 instead of-1. This is outside stage01's added100ns-aligned tests. Stage02 will preserve the1ns Timestamp representation assertions, condition exact1ns SystemTime coverage on representability, and add a100ns negative roundtrip.
